mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 60% of months with rising PAYEMS (month-over-month increase > 0.5%)

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 50% of months when UNRATE < 4.0%

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 245.0) indicates a monetary tightening cycle, which typically pressures equity valuations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL > 245.0

mechanism_narrative: In supply-constrained economies where industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, reduced production capacity leads to higher prices and profit margins for companies, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in > 50% of periods when INDPRO < 100

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP (GDPC1) exceeds 19000 billion dollars, it reflects strong economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in > 50% of months when GDPC1 > 19000

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 1100 thousand units signals robust demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of economic strength and drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in > 55% of months with HOUST > 1100

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 245.0, it indicates moderate inflation that supports corporate pricing power and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in > 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 245.0

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicates a tight labor market that enhances consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are negative in > 55% of months when UNRATE < 4.5%
